import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sphere packing

The sphere packing problem asks for the largest fraction $\Delta_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ that can be
covered by non-overlapping congruent balls. The value of $\Delta_n$ is known only for
$n = 1, 2, 3, 8, 24$. Its value in the remaining dimensions and its asymptotic behaviour as
$n \to \infty$ are open.

A packing of unit balls is described by its set of centres $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, where
distinct centres are at distance at least $2$. Following [Vi17], its (upper) density is
$$\Delta_X = \limsup_{r \to \infty}
  \frac{\mathrm{vol}\big(\bigcup_{x \in X} B(x, 1) \cap B(0, r)\big)}{\mathrm{vol}(B(0, r))}.$$
The sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$ is the supremum of $\Delta_X$ over all packings, and the
lattice sphere packing constant $\Delta_n^{(L)}$ is the supremum over the packings whose centres
form a lattice. Since density is invariant under scaling, fixing the radius to be $1$ loses no
generality.

This file states the following conjectures.

- The Conway–Sloane conjecture that $\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$ for all $n \le 9$ [CoSl95, Sl98].
- The conjecture that in some dimension the densest packing is irregular, i.e.
  $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$ for some $n$.
- The Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound
  $\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim 3.276\ldots \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$, an
  exponential improvement on Minkowski's bound $2^{-n}$ [ToSt06].

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sphere packing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sl98] N. J. A. Sloane, *The Sphere-Packing Problem*, Documenta Mathematica, Extra Volume ICM
  1998, III, 387–396. [arXiv:math/0207256](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207256)
- [CoSl95] J. H. Conway and N. J. A. Sloane, *What are all the best sphere packings in low
  dimensions?*, Discrete Comput. Geom. 13 (1995), 383–403.
- [ToSt06] S. Torquato and F. H. Stillinger, *New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density
  of sphere packings*, Experimental Mathematics 15 (2006), 307–331.
  [arXiv:math/0508381](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508381)
- [Vi17] M. Viazovska, *The sphere packing problem in dimension 8*, Annals of Mathematics 185
  (2017), 991–1015. [arXiv:1603.04246](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.04246)
-/
open MeasureTheory Metric Filter Real
open scoped EuclideanGeometry
namespace SpherePacking
variable {n : ℕ}

blocks.code:
def IsPacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  X.Pairwise fun x y => 2 ≤ dist x y
blocks.docstring:
A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a (unit) sphere packing if any two
distinct points of `X` are at distance at least `2`, i.e. the open unit balls centred at the points
of `X` are pairwise disjoint.

justification.closest_existing_considered: SquarePacking.Packing (finite packings in ℝ², bounded container); Metric.ball / Set.Pairwise.
justification.name: SpherePacking.IsPacking
justification.why_needed: No notion of a sphere packing (set of centres with pairwise distance ≥ 2) exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib; the repo's `SquarePacking.Packing` only handles finitely many isometric copies inside a bounded container in ℝ².

blocks.name: IsPacking
blocks.text:
/--
A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a (unit) sphere packing if any two
distinct points of `X` are at distance at least `2`, i.e. the open unit balls centred at the points
of `X` are pairwise disjoint.
-/
def IsPacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  X.Pairwise fun x y => 2 ≤ dist x y

blocks.code:
def IsLatticePacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  IsPacking X ∧
    ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L),
      IsZLattice ℝ L ∧ (L : Set (ℝ^n)) = X
blocks.docstring:
A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a lattice sphere packing if it is
the set of centres of a sphere packing and it is a (full rank) lattice in $\mathbb{R}^n$, i.e. a
discrete additive subgroup spanning $\mathbb{R}^n$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsZLattice (Mathlib) — used as the lattice notion; there is no existing combination with a minimal-distance/packing condition.
justification.name: SpherePacking.IsLatticePacking
justification.why_needed: Needed to define the lattice packing constant Δ_n^{(L)}: a packing whose centre set is a full-rank lattice.

blocks.name: IsLatticePacking
blocks.text:
/--
A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a lattice sphere packing if it is
the set of centres of a sphere packing and it is a (full rank) lattice in $\mathbb{R}^n$, i.e. a
discrete additive subgroup spanning $\mathbb{R}^n$.
-/
def IsLatticePacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  IsPacking X ∧
    ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L),
      IsZLattice ℝ L ∧ (L : Set (ℝ^n)) = X

blocks.code:
noncomputable def finiteDensity (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (volume ((⋃ x ∈ X, ball x 1) ∩ ball 0 r)).toReal / (volume (ball (0 : ℝ^n) r)).toReal
blocks.docstring:
The finite density of the packing with centres `X` at radius `r`: the fraction of the ball of
radius `r` around the origin that is covered by the open unit balls centred at the points of `X`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MeasureTheory.volume, EuclideanSpace.volume_ball (used), ZLattice.covolume (only for lattices, not general packings).
justification.name: SpherePacking.finiteDensity
justification.why_needed: The fraction of the ball B(0,r) covered by the packing; building block for the density. Mathlib has no packing-density notion.

blocks.name: finiteDensity
blocks.text:
/--
The finite density of the packing with centres `X` at radius `r`: the fraction of the ball of
radius `r` around the origin that is covered by the open unit balls centred at the points of `X`.
-/
noncomputable def finiteDensity (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (volume ((⋃ x ∈ X, ball x 1) ∩ ball 0 r)).toReal / (volume (ball (0 : ℝ^n) r)).toReal

blocks.code:
noncomputable def density (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : ℝ :=
  limsup (finiteDensity X) atTop
blocks.docstring:
The density of the packing with centres `X`, defined as the limit superior of the finite densities
as the radius tends to infinity, as in [Vi17].

justification.closest_existing_considered: Filter.limsup (used); no packing-density definition exists in Mathlib.
justification.name: SpherePacking.density
justification.why_needed: The asymptotic density of a packing (limsup of finite densities), the quantity whose supremum defines Δ_n.

blocks.name: density
blocks.text:
/--
The density of the packing with centres `X`, defined as the limit superior of the finite densities
as the radius tends to infinity, as in [Vi17].
-/
noncomputable def density (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : ℝ :=
  limsup (finiteDensity X) atTop

blocks.code:
noncomputable def packingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsPacking X})
blocks.docstring:
The sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$: the supremum of the densities of all sphere packings in
$\mathbb{R}^n$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib/FormalConjecturesForMathlib; Green42.CohnElkiesOptimal concerns the Cohn–Elkies LP bound, not Δ_n.
justification.name: SpherePacking.packingConstant
justification.why_needed: The sphere packing constant Δ_n = sup over all packings in ℝ^n; central object of all three slots.

blocks.name: packingConstant
blocks.text:
/--
The sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$: the supremum of the densities of all sphere packings in
$\mathbb{R}^n$.
-/
noncomputable def packingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsPacking X})

noncomputable def latticePackingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsLatticePacking X})
blocks.docstring:
The lattice sphere packing constant $\Delta_n^{(L)}$: the supremum of the densities of all lattice
sphere packings in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Hermite constant is not in Mathlib; ZLattice.covolume exists but no density/supremum notion.
justification.name: SpherePacking.latticePackingConstant
justification.why_needed: The lattice sphere packing constant Δ_n^{(L)} = sup over lattice packings, needed for slots 1 and 2.

blocks.text:
/--
The lattice sphere packing constant $\Delta_n^{(L)}$: the supremum of the densities of all lattice

noncomputable def latticePackingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 11 52]
theorem latticePackingConstant_le_packingConstant (n : ℕ) :
    latticePackingConstant n ≤ packingConstant n := by
  by_cases h : ∃ X : Set (ℝ^n), IsLatticePacking X
  · refine csSup_le_csSup ⟨1, ?_⟩ (h.elim fun X hX => ⟨_, X, hX, rfl⟩)
      (Set.image_mono fun X hX => hX.1)
    rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩
    exact density_le_one X
  · push_neg at h
    have : {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsLatticePacking X} = ∅ := Set.eq_empty_of_forall_notMem h
    simp only [latticePackingConstant, this, Set.image_empty, Real.sSup_empty]
    exact packingConstant_nonneg n
blocks.docstring: Every lattice packing is a packing, so $\Delta_n^{(L)} \le \Delta_n$.
blocks.name: latticePackingConstant_le_packingConstant
blocks.text:
/-- Every lattice packing is a packing, so $\Delta_n^{(L)} \le \Delta_n$. -/
@[category API, AMS 11 52]
theorem latticePackingConstant_le_packingConstant (n : ℕ) :
    latticePackingConstant n ≤ packingConstant n := by
  by_cases h : ∃ X : Set (ℝ^n), IsLatticePacking X
  · refine csSup_le_csSup ⟨1, ?_⟩ (h.elim fun X hX => ⟨_, X, hX, rfl⟩)
      (Set.image_mono fun X hX => hX.1)
    rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩
    exact density_le_one X
  · push_neg at h
    have : {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsLatticePacking X} = ∅ := Set.eq_empty_of_forall_notMem h
    simp only [latticePackingConstant, this, Set.image_empty, Real.sSup_empty]
    exact packingConstant_nonneg n

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 9) :
    packingConstant n = latticePackingConstant n := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Conway–Sloane conjecture** [CoSl95, Sl98]: for every dimension $1 \le n \le 9$ the densest
sphere packing in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is no denser than the densest lattice packing, i.e.
$\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$.

The densest lattice packings are known for $n \le 8$ (the root lattices
$A_1, A_2, A_3, D_4, D_5, E_6, E_7, E_8$), while $\Delta_9^{(L)}$ is unknown. The optimal packing
among all packings is known only in dimensions $1, 2, 3, 8$ and $24$, where it is a lattice
packing, so the conjecture is known for $n = 1, 2, 3, 8$ and open for $n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 9$. In
the open cases $n = 4, 5, 6, 7$ the conjecture asserts that $\Delta_n$ equals the density of
$D_4, D_5, E_6, E_7$ respectively, namely $\pi^2/16$, $\pi^2/(15\sqrt{2})$,
$\pi^3/(48\sqrt{3})$, $\pi^3/105$.

@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, latticePackingConstant n < packingConstant n := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
It is possible that in some dimension the densest sphere packing is irregular (that is, not a
lattice packing): there is some $n$ with $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$.

Some support for this comes from dimension $10$, where the densest known packing, the
non-lattice packing $P_{10c}$ of Best, is denser than the densest known lattice packing [Sl98].

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6) * 2 ^ (-((3 - logb 2 (exp 1)) * n / 2)) ≤
        packingConstant n := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound** [ToSt06, Section 5]: for large $n$,
$$\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim \frac{3.276100896 \cdot n^{1/6}}{2^{0.7786524795\ldots n}},$$
where the exponent is exactly $(3 - \log_2 e)/2$. This would be an exponential improvement on
Minkowski's lower bound $\Delta_n \ge 2^{-n}$. The bound is conditional on the conjecture of
[ToSt06] characterising the pair correlation functions of disordered sphere packings in high
dimensions.

Since the leading constant is only determined numerically, we state the bound with an unspecified
positive constant $c$: there is $c > 0$ such that
$\Delta_n \ge c \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
blocks.name: sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound

claims.decomposer_note: Asks to determine the value of the optimal packing density Δ_n (supremum of upper densities over all packings of congruent balls in ℝ^n, not just lattice packings) for every n ∉ {1,2,3,8,24}; no candidate value is asserted for general n (the article even suggests the optimum may be non-lattice in some dimensions), so the deliverable is a value with no Prop to state, except for the n ≤ 9 special case with the Conway–Sloane candidate recorded in the next entry.
claims.source_text: the density of the densest packing in dimensions other than 1, 2, 3, 8 and 24
claims.text_span: the density of the densest packing in dimensions other than 1, 2, 3, 8 and 24

claims.decomposer_note: The candidate answer for the remaining low dimensions asserted in the cited Sloane 1998 ICM paper (Conway–Sloane conjecture): Δ_n = Δ_n^{(L)} for all n ≤ 9, i.e. the densest packing density equals the densest lattice packing density (sup over lattice packings); open content is n = 4,5,6,7 (D4, D5, E6, E7 with densities π²/16, π²/(15√2), π³/(48√3), π³/105) and n = 9 (where Δ_9^{(L)} is itself unknown, so phrase via the lattice supremum rather than explicit values); cases n = 1,2,3,8 are known true.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state Sloane's (ICM 1998, quoting Conway–Sloane 1995) conjecture Δ_n = Δ_n^{(L)} via suprema of upper densities; I used c07's definitions (repo `ℝ^n` notation, Mathlib `IsZLattice` for full-rank discrete ℤ-submodules, Viazovska's limsup density, real `sSup` over nonempty sets bounded by 1, with proven API lemmas 0 ≤ Δ_n^{(L)} ≤ Δ_n ≤ 1) but restricted the quantifier to `n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 9` (as in c01/c03/c05) instead of c07's `n ≤ 9`, so that the degenerate dimension 0 is not part of the statement. Cases 1,2,3,8 are known and included as in the source's 'for n ≤ 9'.
claims.source_text: The densest lattice packings of hyperspheres are known for 1–8 and 24 dimensions. Comparatively little is known about non-lattice hypersphere packings, the optimal result being known only in dimensions 1–3, 8, and 24
claims.text_span: The densest lattice packings of hyperspheres are known for 1–8 and 24 dimensions. Comparatively little is known about non-lattice hypersphere packings, the optimal result being known only in dimensions 1–3, 8, and 24

claims.decomposer_note: 'Irregular' means non-lattice in the article's terminology, so the Prop is ∃ n, Δ_n^{(L)} < Δ_n (sup of lattice packing densities strictly below sup over all packings in ℝ^n; phrasing via sups avoids attainment issues); the cited Cohn–Kumar paper states the stronger form 'lattices are suboptimal in all sufficiently high dimensions' (∀ᶠ n, Δ_n^{(L)} < Δ_n), which is a possible stronger sub-variant; the article's evidence (dimension 10, P10c) is not itself a proof.
claims.reviewer_why: `∃ n, latticePackingConstant n < packingConstant n`, strict inequality of suprema (no attainment). No spurious witness at n = 0: in ℝ^0 the only packings are ∅ and {0}, {0} is a lattice packing, and density ∅ = 0 ≤ density {0}, so both suprema coincide there regardless of measure conventions. Candidates c02/c04/c06/c08 add `0 < n`, which is equivalent; I kept the notes' literal form.
claims.source_text: it is possible that in some dimensions the densest packing may be irregular

claims.decomposer_note: Asks to determine the growth rate of Δ_n as n → ∞ ('its' = the densest packing density over all packings, although the article's θ(n) paragraph is about the densest lattice); known results c·n²·2^{-n} ≤ Δ_n^{(L)} ≤ Δ_n ≤ 2^{-(0.599…+o(1))n} are solved, and no candidate for the actual rate (not even the exponential rate lim (1/n)log₂Δ_n, whose existence is unknown) is asserted; Venkatesh's conjecture Δ_n^{(L)} ≤ n²(log n)^{O(1)}2^{-n} (quoted in the cited Klartag and Elisha–Gargava–Zhao papers) is a candidate only for the lattice-restricted variant, not for the statement's question.

context:
In geometry, a sphere packing is an arrangement of non-overlapping spheres within a containing space. The spheres considered are usually all of identical size, and the space is usually three-dimensional Euclidean space. However, sphere packing problems can be generalised to consider unequal spheres, spaces of other dimensions (where the problem becomes circle packing in two dimensions, or hypersphere packing in higher dimensions) or to non-Euclidean spaces such as hyperbolic space.
A typical sphere packing problem is to find an arrangement in which the spheres fill as much of the space as possible. The proportion of space filled by the spheres is called the packing density of the arrangement. As the local density of a packing in an infinite space can vary depending on the volume over which it is measured, the problem is usually to maximise the average or asymptotic density, measured over a large enough volume.
For equal spheres in three dimensions, the densest packing uses approximately 74% of the volume. A random packing of equal spheres generally has a density around 63.5%.

decomposition_objections.text: None of substance. Minor remark: the Wikipedia article is internally inconsistent about 'regular' (it calls HCP 'a regular arrangement' that is 'not a lattice'), but the decomposition's reading of 'irregular' as 'non-lattice' matches the article's definition sentence and the dimension-10 evidence, and I followed it.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sphere packing

The sphere packing problem asks for the largest fraction $\Delta_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ that can be
covered by non-overlapping congruent balls. The value of $\Delta_n$ is known only for
$n = 1, 2, 3, 8, 24$. Its value in the remaining dimensions and its asymptotic behaviour as
$n \to \infty$ are open.

A packing of unit balls is described by its set of centres $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, where
distinct centres are at distance at least $2$. Following [Vi17], its (upper) density is
$$\Delta_X = \limsup_{r \to \infty}
  \frac{\mathrm{vol}\big(\bigcup_{x \in X} B(x, 1) \cap B(0, r)\big)}{\mathrm{vol}(B(0, r))}.$$
The sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$ is the supremum of $\Delta_X$ over all packings, and the
lattice sphere packing constant $\Delta_n^{(L)}$ is the supremum over the packings whose centres
form a lattice. Since density is invariant under scaling, fixing the radius to be $1$ loses no
generality.

This file states the following conjectures.

- The Conway–Sloane conjecture that $\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$ for all $n \le 9$ [CoSl95, Sl98].
- The conjecture that in some dimension the densest packing is irregular, i.e.
  $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$ for some $n$.
- The Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound
  $\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim 3.276\ldots \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$, an
  exponential improvement on Minkowski's bound $2^{-n}$ [ToSt06].

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sphere packing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sl98] N. J. A. Sloane, *The Sphere-Packing Problem*, Documenta Mathematica, Extra Volume ICM
  1998, III, 387–396. [arXiv:math/0207256](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207256)
- [CoSl95] J. H. Conway and N. J. A. Sloane, *What are all the best sphere packings in low
  dimensions?*, Discrete Comput. Geom. 13 (1995), 383–403.
- [ToSt06] S. Torquato and F. H. Stillinger, *New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density
  of sphere packings*, Experimental Mathematics 15 (2006), 307–331.
  [arXiv:math/0508381](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508381)
- [Vi17] M. Viazovska, *The sphere packing problem in dimension 8*, Annals of Mathematics 185
  (2017), 991–1015. [arXiv:1603.04246](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.04246)
-/

open MeasureTheory Metric Filter Real
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace SpherePacking

variable {n : ℕ}

/--
A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a (unit) sphere packing if any two
distinct points of `X` are at distance at least `2`, i.e. the open unit balls centred at the points
of `X` are pairwise disjoint.
-/
def IsPacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  X.Pairwise fun x y => 2 ≤ dist x y

/--
A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a lattice sphere packing if it is
the set of centres of a sphere packing and it is a (full rank) lattice in $\mathbb{R}^n$, i.e. a
discrete additive subgroup spanning $\mathbb{R}^n$.
-/
def IsLatticePacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  IsPacking X ∧
    ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L),
      IsZLattice ℝ L ∧ (L : Set (ℝ^n)) = X

/--
The finite density of the packing with centres `X` at radius `r`: the fraction of the ball of
radius `r` around the origin that is covered by the open unit balls centred at the points of `X`.
-/
noncomputable def finiteDensity (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (volume ((⋃ x ∈ X, ball x 1) ∩ ball 0 r)).toReal / (volume (ball (0 : ℝ^n) r)).toReal

/--
The density of the packing with centres `X`, defined as the limit superior of the finite densities
as the radius tends to infinity, as in [Vi17].
-/
noncomputable def density (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : ℝ :=
  limsup (finiteDensity X) atTop

/--
The sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$: the supremum of the densities of all sphere packings in
$\mathbb{R}^n$.
-/
noncomputable def packingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsPacking X})

/--
The lattice sphere packing constant $\Delta_n^{(L)}$: the supremum of the densities of all lattice
sphere packings in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
-/
noncomputable def latticePackingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsLatticePacking X})

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem finiteDensity_nonneg (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (r : ℝ) : 0 ≤ finiteDensity X r := by
  unfold finiteDensity
  positivity

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem finiteDensity_le_one (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (r : ℝ) : finiteDensity X r ≤ 1 :=
  div_le_one_of_le₀
    (ENNReal.toReal_mono measure_ball_lt_top.ne (measure_mono Set.inter_subset_right))
    ENNReal.toReal_nonneg

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem density_nonneg (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : 0 ≤ density X :=
  le_limsup_of_frequently_le (Frequently.of_forall (finiteDensity_nonneg X))
    (isBoundedUnder_of ⟨1, finiteDensity_le_one X⟩)

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem density_le_one (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : density X ≤ 1 :=
  limsup_le_of_le (isCoboundedUnder_le_of_le _ (finiteDensity_nonneg X))
    (Eventually.of_forall (finiteDensity_le_one X))

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isPacking_empty : IsPacking (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) :=
  Set.pairwise_empty _

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem density_empty : density (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) = 0 := by
  have : finiteDensity (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) = fun _ => 0 := by
    ext r
    simp [finiteDensity]
  rw [density, this, limsup_const]

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem packingConstant_nonneg (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ packingConstant n :=
  le_csSup_of_le ⟨1, by rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩; exact density_le_one X⟩
    ⟨∅, isPacking_empty, rfl⟩ (density_nonneg _)

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem packingConstant_le_one (n : ℕ) : packingConstant n ≤ 1 :=
  csSup_le ⟨_, ∅, isPacking_empty, rfl⟩ (by rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩; exact density_le_one X)

/-- Every lattice packing is a packing, so $\Delta_n^{(L)} \le \Delta_n$. -/
@[category API, AMS 11 52]
theorem latticePackingConstant_le_packingConstant (n : ℕ) :
    latticePackingConstant n ≤ packingConstant n := by
  by_cases h : ∃ X : Set (ℝ^n), IsLatticePacking X
  · refine csSup_le_csSup ⟨1, ?_⟩ (h.elim fun X hX => ⟨_, X, hX, rfl⟩)
      (Set.image_mono fun X hX => hX.1)
    rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩
    exact density_le_one X
  · push_neg at h
    have : {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsLatticePacking X} = ∅ := Set.eq_empty_of_forall_notMem h
    simp only [latticePackingConstant, this, Set.image_empty, Real.sSup_empty]
    exact packingConstant_nonneg n

/--
**Conway–Sloane conjecture** [CoSl95, Sl98]: for every dimension $1 \le n \le 9$ the densest
sphere packing in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is no denser than the densest lattice packing, i.e.
$\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$.

The densest lattice packings are known for $n \le 8$ (the root lattices
$A_1, A_2, A_3, D_4, D_5, E_6, E_7, E_8$), while $\Delta_9^{(L)}$ is unknown. The optimal packing
among all packings is known only in dimensions $1, 2, 3, 8$ and $24$, where it is a lattice
packing, so the conjecture is known for $n = 1, 2, 3, 8$ and open for $n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 9$. In
the open cases $n = 4, 5, 6, 7$ the conjecture asserts that $\Delta_n$ equals the density of
$D_4, D_5, E_6, E_7$ respectively, namely $\pi^2/16$, $\pi^2/(15\sqrt{2})$,
$\pi^3/(48\sqrt{3})$, $\pi^3/105$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 9) :
    packingConstant n = latticePackingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
It is possible that in some dimension the densest sphere packing is irregular (that is, not a
lattice packing): there is some $n$ with $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$.

Some support for this comes from dimension $10$, where the densest known packing, the
non-lattice packing $P_{10c}$ of Best, is denser than the densest known lattice packing [Sl98].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, latticePackingConstant n < packingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
**Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound** [ToSt06, Section 5]: for large $n$,
$$\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim \frac{3.276100896 \cdot n^{1/6}}{2^{0.7786524795\ldots n}},$$
where the exponent is exactly $(3 - \log_2 e)/2$. This would be an exponential improvement on
Minkowski's lower bound $\Delta_n \ge 2^{-n}$. The bound is conditional on the conjecture of
[ToSt06] characterising the pair correlation functions of disordered sphere packings in high
dimensions.

Since the leading constant is only determined numerically, we state the bound with an unspecified
positive constant $c$: there is $c > 0$ such that
$\Delta_n \ge c \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6) * 2 ^ (-((3 - logb 2 (exp 1)) * n / 2)) ≤
        packingConstant n := by
  sorry

end SpherePacking

items: Packings are normalised to unit radius: `IsPacking X` means the centre set X ⊆ ℝ^n is pairwise at distance ≥ 2 (equivalently the open unit balls are disjoint). Density is scale-invariant so this loses no generality (Viazovska's and Torquato–Stillinger's conventions differ only by scaling).

Density of a packing is defined as in Viazovska 2017: limsup as r → ∞ of vol(P ∩ B(0,r))/vol(B(0,r)) with P the union of the open unit balls. Finite densities lie in [0,1] (proved as API lemmas), so the real-valued `limsup` has no junk value. Conway–Sloane/Wikipedia do not fix a precise definition; the supremum over packings is the same for all standard choices (balls vs cubes, limsup vs lim over packings for which the limit exists).

Δ_n and Δ_n^{(L)} are `sSup` of the image of `density` over all packings / all lattice packings. Both sets are nonempty (∅ is a packing; 2ℤ^n is a lattice packing) and bounded by 1, so `sSup` is the true supremum. `latticePackingConstant_le_packingConstant` is proved as API.

Lattice packings use Mathlib's `IsZLattice ℝ L` (discrete ℤ-submodule spanning ℝ^n) for `L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)` with `(L : Set) = X`; the `DiscreteTopology L` instance is existentially quantified in the definition. Density of a lattice packing is computed by the same limsup definition rather than vol(ball)/covolume; these agree mathematically.

Slot 1 is stated for all n ≤ 9 including the degenerate n = 0 (ℝ^0 is a point): there the only packings are ∅ and {0}, {0} is a lattice packing, and both constants equal density {0}, so the equality holds trivially and no positivity hypothesis was added.

'Irregular' in slot 2 is interpreted as 'non-lattice', following the article's own gloss (a lattice arrangement is 'commonly called a regular arrangement') and the decomposition notes; the article's evidence about dimension 10 compares against the densest known *lattice* packing.

Slot 3 replaces the numerically determined constant 3.276100896 by an unspecified c > 0 (the paper's statement Δ_n ≥ φ_* ∼ C n^{1/6} 2^{-αn} implies the stated form for every c < C). The exponent uses `logb 2 (exp 1)` for log₂ e; Real.rpow is used throughout with n cast to ℝ.

Extra declarations beyond the three slots: the Cohn–Kumar eventual form of slot 2, the ε-weak form of slot 3, and `research solved` statements Δ_3 = π/√18 (Hales), Δ_8 = π⁴/384 (Viazovska), Δ_24 = π¹²/12! (CKMRV), plus API/test lemmas (bounds 0 ≤ density ≤ 1, empty packing, Δ_n^{(L)} ≤ Δ_n) that exercise the definitions.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates compiled and were mutually consistent on all three slots; differences were only in definitional style (volume-based vs. c02's center-counting density; IsZLattice vs. ℤ-span of a basis; ℝ vs. c08's ℝ≥0∞ codomain; c06's unit-diameter normalization), all mathematically equivalent for the suprema. Final file is built on c07 (most complete proven API/test lemmas, repository `ℝ^n` idiom). Edits: Conway–Sloane slot restricted to 1 ≤ n ≤ 9; module docstring trimmed; the extra declarations present in several candidates (Cohn–Kumar eventual form of irregularity, ε-weak form of the TS bound, and 'research solved' values Δ_3, Δ_8, Δ_24) were NOT shipped since the instruction is to ship exactly the surviving slots — they looked faithful and could be added later. Caveats a human should know: (1) the 'sphere_packing' slot's text span is a statement of known facts; per the decomposition notes it is formalized as the cited Conway–Sloane conjecture, which includes the already-proved cases n = 1,2,3,8 alongside the open n = 4–7, 9. (2) The TS bound is a conjectural consequence of their pair-correlation Conjecture 1, not a theorem-style conjecture; the docstring records this and the category is research open. (3) 'Irregular' is read as 'non-lattice' following the article's own definition sentence; the Wikipedia article is loose about 'regular' elsewhere (it calls HCP a regular non-lattice arrangement). (4) Density is upper density (limsup) over origin-centred balls with unit radius normalization; the supremum is insensitive to these standard choices (Groemer), but a reviewer wanting the classical lim-based definition should note the difference is immaterial only at the level of Δ_n.
